questions.q: According to this lesson, why does 'it works in dev, fails in prod' usually happen?
options: Dev and prod were provisioned and configured by hand, at different times, and quietly drifted apart in undocumented ways
It is always caused by a bug in the application code itself
Dev environments are always slower than prod, which is the only possible cause
It happens randomly and has no real underlying explanation
questions.explain: The lesson attributes this specifically to manual, untracked configuration drift between environments built separately.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of environment drift this lesson gives?
options: max server memory was bumped on prod during an incident and never mirrored to dev
Prod has more RAM than dev, which is expected and by design
The application code was updated in a pull request
A user's password expired
questions.explain: That's the lesson's exact example of an undocumented manual change that causes silent drift.

questions.q: How does a parameterized IaC template solve the environment-drift problem?
options: The same source file provisions dev, test, and prod, varying only specific inputs like SKU size, so everything else stays structurally identical
It automatically copies production data into dev on every deploy
It prevents any DBA from ever making manual changes to a server, at the OS level
It merges dev, test, and prod into a single shared environment
questions.explain: One template with different variable inputs per environment removes the separate, driftable manual setup steps.

questions.q: What does the lesson say environment consistency from IaC does NOT guarantee?
options: That data and load will be the same across environments, or that nobody manually changes something afterward
That two environments provisioned from the same template will have any structural similarity at all
That the template can be version controlled
That the template can be parameterized
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that structural consistency at provisioning time is not the same as identical data, load, or freedom from later manual drift.

questions.q: What catches drift introduced by someone manually changing a setting AFTER an environment was consistently provisioned?
options: Re-applying a declarative configuration-as-code resource on a schedule, as covered in the previous lesson
Re-running terraform plan has no way to detect this at all, ever
Only a full server rebuild can catch this
Nothing can catch this kind of drift
questions.explain: The lesson ties this back to configuration as code (Lesson 25) — reconciling declared state on a schedule catches later manual drift.
